## 結論：不是 build 失敗，是 GitHub Pages 部署卡住了

你的 commit（`feat(shell): frictionless copilot-proxy enable/disable for Claude Code`）觸發的 Docs workflow 有兩個 job：

| Job | 結果 | 說明 |
|---|---|---|
| **build** | ✅ 成功 (33s) | `mkdocs build` 正常，artifact 也上傳了 |
| **deploy** | ❌ 失敗 (10m) | `actions/deploy-pages@v5` 超時 |

### 失敗原因

deploy job 的 log 從頭到尾就是這一句重複了 120 次：

```
Getting Pages deployment status...
Current status: deployment_queued
...
##[error]Timeout reached, aborting!
Canceling Pages deployment...
```

部署一直卡在 **`deployment_queued`**（排隊中），10 分鐘（action 預設 `timeout: 600000`ms）內都沒有變成 `deployment_success`，於是 action 主動 abort。

**這是 GitHub Pages 後端的暫時性壅塞/降級，不是你的程式或設定問題。** 佐證：

- build 完全正常，artifact（`artifact_id: 8044709046`）有成功建立。
- **上一次成功的 run，deploy 就已經花了 7m52s** — 正常 `deploy-pages` 只要 30–60 秒。可見那時 Pages 後端就在變慢，這次直接越過 10 分鐘的 timeout 線。
- 你的 `docs.yml` 設定沒問題（標準的 build → upload-pages-artifact → deploy-pages 三段式，權限 `pages: write` + `id-token: write` 都齊）。

### 建議做法

最直接的是**重跑失敗的 deploy job**（程式沒問題，重試通常就過）。要我幫你重跑嗎？

```bash
gh run rerun 28604400648 --repo daviddwlee84/dotfiles --failed
```

> 注意 workflow 有 `concurrency: group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false`，重跑前先確認沒有另一個 Docs run 正在跑，否則新的會排在後面等。

---

如果這種排隊超時**反覆發生**，可以考慮把 deploy 的 timeout 調長（減少誤判），例如：

```yaml
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
        with:
          timeout: 1200000   # 20 min，預設是 10 min
```

要我直接幫你重跑，還是順便把 `docs.yml` 的 timeout 調長？

```text
1	# Copilot → Claude Code proxy
2	
3	Back [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) with the
4	**Claude models from a GitHub Copilot subscription**, via a local
5	reverse-engineered proxy ([`ericc-ch/copilot-api`](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api)).
6	
7	- **Shell helpers**: `~/.config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` (`copilot-proxy`, `claude-copilot`, `copilot-run`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model`)
8	- **Runner**: `bunx copilot-api` (pinned; matches the `bunx` convention in `07_bunx_cli.sh`)
9	- **Not installed by ansible** — pulled on demand via `bunx`, so it stays off the
10	  provisioning path.
11	
12	!!! warning "This violates GitHub Copilot's Terms of Service"
13	    Using a Copilot subscription to power a non-GitHub agent is not permitted, and
14	    copilot-api is reverse-engineered/unofficial. copilot-api's own README warns it
15	    can trigger GitHub's **abuse detection** and lead to **temporary suspension of
16	    Copilot access**. Claude Code is token-hungry (frequent background calls, large
17	    context) — always run with a rate limit. Use at your own risk; prefer a personal
18	    account over a corporate seat.
19	
20	## Quick start
21	
22	```sh
23	copilot-proxy auth      # one-time: GitHub device login (stores a ghu_ token)
24	
25	claude-copilot          # one-off session on the proxy (auto-starts it; no file writes)
26	
27	copilot-here on         # OR: pin THIS project — plain `claude` uses the proxy
28	copilot-here off        # unpin — back to the real Anthropic backend
29	```
30	
31	## How it works
32	
33	```
34	Claude Code ──Anthropic /v1/messages──▶ copilot-api (localhost:4141)
35	                                          │ translates Anthropic <-> Copilot
36	                                          │ Authorization: Bearer <copilot token>
37	                                          ▼
38	                                   api.githubcopilot.com  (your Copilot sub)
39	```
40	
41	- Claude Code speaks only the **Anthropic Messages API** (`/v1/messages`).
42	- Copilot's chat endpoint is **OpenAI-compatible** (`/chat/completions`).
43	- copilot-api translates between them and injects the Copilot auth.
44	- Claude Code is pointed at the proxy via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` — injected either
45	  as per-process env (`claude-copilot`) or via the gitignored
46	  `./.claude/settings.local.json` (`copilot-here on`). See "Settings-layer design".
47	
48	## Settings-layer design (which file gets the proxy config, and why)
49	
50	Claude Code merges settings low → high: `~/.claude/settings.json` (user) →
51	`./.claude/settings.json` (project, committed) → `./.claude/settings.local.json`
52	(local, gitignored) → CLI flags — and **shell env vars beat the `env` block of
53	every settings file** ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings)).
54	
55	Two of those layers are already owned by other tooling and must stay clean:
56	
57	| Layer | Owner | Why proxy config must NOT go here |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| `~/.claude/settings.json` | chezmoi (`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`) | always-on for *every* project; fights the chezmoi merge |
60	| `./.claude/settings.json` | `claude-plans-here` (`plansDirectory`) | committed to git — proxy config would leak to the team |
61	
62	So the proxy uses the two layers nobody else owns:
63	
64	| Enable | Mechanism | Scope | Disable |
65	|---|---|---|---|
66	| `claude-copilot` / `copilot-run` | per-process env vars | one session | just run plain `claude` next time |
67	| `copilot-here on` | `./.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) | this project, sticky | `copilot-here off` |
68	
69	```
70	~/.claude/settings.json          .claude/settings.json         .claude/settings.local.json      shell env
71	(chezmoi: hooks/plugins)    <    (git: plansDirectory)     <   (copilot-here on/off)        <   (claude-copilot)
72	```
73	
74	## Shell helpers
75	
76	### `copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|logs [N]|whoami|auth]`
77	
78	Manages the background proxy on `$COPILOT_PROXY_PORT` (default `4141`).
79	
80	| Env var | Default | Meaning |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `COPILOT_PROXY_PORT` | `4141` | port the proxy listens on |
83	| `COPILOT_PROXY_RATE` | `15` | `--rate-limit` seconds (throttle; be gentle) |
84	| `COPILOT_API_PKG` | `copilot-api@0.7.0` | `bunx` package spec (pin / upgrade) |
85	
86	Set these in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` (or the per-shell secrets files). `start` refuses
87	to run until `copilot-proxy auth` has stored a token, and waits up to ~20s for the
88	proxy to answer before returning.
89	
90	`copilot-proxy whoami` is the real login check: it exchanges the stored token
91	against GitHub and prints your account / plan / quota (fails loudly if the token
92	is missing or expired). Use it instead of eyeballing the token file — the token
93	is a plaintext credential and should not be opened in an editor.
94	
95	### `claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]` — one-off session
96	
97	Layer 1: run a single Claude Code session on the proxy with **zero file
98	writes**. Auto-starts the proxy if it isn't answering, then launches `claude`
99	with the `ANTHROPIC_*` env injected per-process (shell env beats every
100	settings-file `env` block, so this wins even where `copilot-here` is off).
101	
102	- Wraps in `specstory run claude` when specstory is installed (markdown
103	  auto-save — same convention as `scode`/`svibe`); opt out with
104	  `--no-specstory`. Extra args reach the claude CLI via specstory's
105	  `-c "custom command"` passthrough: `claude-copilot -c` → continue session.
106	- Revert = nothing to revert; plain `claude` next time is untouched.
107	
108	### `copilot-run <cmd...>` — generic env injector
109	
110	The building block under `claude-copilot`: auto-starts the proxy and runs *any*
111	command with the proxy env. Useful for other Anthropic-compatible tools or a
112	custom specstory invocation:
113	
114	```sh
115	copilot-run specstory run claude    # exactly what claude-copilot does
116	copilot-run claude --resume         # raw claude, no specstory
117	```
118	
119	### `copilot-here [on|off|status]` — sticky per-project toggle
120	
121	Layer 2: pin **this project** to the proxy via `./.claude/settings.local.json`
122	so plain `claude` (and `scode`/`svibe` panes, which just run
123	`specstory run claude`) uses the proxy until you turn it off. Requires `jq`.
124	
125	- `on` — jq-merges the proxy `env` block into `settings.local.json` (creates it
126	  if missing) and makes sure git ignores the file (via `.git/info/exclude`;
127	  Claude Code only auto-gitignores files *it* creates). The committed
128	  `.claude/settings.json` (`plansDirectory` etc.) is never touched.
129	- `off` — removes exactly the env keys `on` added; other content you put in
130	  `settings.local.json` survives, and the file is deleted if it becomes empty.
131	- `status` — pinned? which base URL / model? warns when the proxy isn't running.
132	
133	### `copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c]`
134	
135	Switches the pinned Copilot model. Requires `jq`. Write target — never the
136	committed `.claude/settings.json`:
137	
138	- `copilot-here` is ON in the current project → edits
139	  `./.claude/settings.local.json`.
140	- otherwise → writes the global state file
141	  `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model`, which `claude-copilot`, `copilot-run`
142	  and the next `copilot-here on` pick up. (`$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` overrides
143	  the state file; final fallback is `claude-opus-4.8`.)
144	
145	Behavior:
146	
147	- Fuzzy id: `copilot-model opus-4.8` resolves to `claude-opus-4.8`.
148	- Validated against the live proxy `/v1/models` (falls back to a static Claude
149	  list if the proxy is down); typos and ambiguous prefixes are rejected.
150	- No argument → `fzf` picker. `-c` prints the current model and which layer it
151	  came from.
152	- Writes both `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` and `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` —
153	  **the change only takes effect on the next `claude` launch** (env is read at
154	  startup). Switching model does **not** require restarting the proxy.
155	
156	## Injected env (what both layers set)
157	
158	```json
159	{
160	  "env": {
161	    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:4141",
162	    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "dummy",
163	    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "claude-opus-4.8",
164	    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "claude-opus-4.8",
165	    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "claude-sonnet-5",
166	    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "claude-haiku-4.5",
167	    "ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL": "claude-haiku-4.5",
168	    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": "1"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is ignored by the proxy but must be set.
174	`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` cuts background chatter (helps with
175	rate limits). Do **not** paste this into the committed `.claude/settings.json` —
176	use `copilot-here on` instead.
177	
178	## Gotchas (these cost real debugging time)
179	
180	### Do not use Claude Code's `/model` picker
181	
182	It sends Anthropic's *official* ids (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8-YYYYMMDD`), but the
183	Copilot backend only knows its own ids (`claude-opus-4.8`). Picking from the menu
184	produces:
185	
186	```
187	API Error: 400 {"error":{"message":"The requested model is not supported.",
188	"code":"model_not_supported", ...}}
189	```
190	
191	Pin the model with `copilot-model` instead.
192	
193	### The "Opus 4 retired" warning is cosmetic
194	
195	Claude Code shows `[Opus 4]` and warns *"Claude Opus 4 was retired"* — it fails to
196	match the Copilot id against its built-in Anthropic table and falls back to the
197	nearest known (retired) name. Requests are still routed correctly to
198	`claude-opus-4.8`. There is no clean way to remove the warning; ignore it.
199	
200	### The token gotcha: `gho_` vs `ghu_`
201	
202	There are two different GitHub tokens, and they are **not** interchangeable:
203	
204	| Source | Prefix | `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange |
205	|---|---|---|
206	| OpenCode's stored auth | `gho_` | **fails (404)** |
207	| `copilot-proxy auth` (device login) | `ghu_` | **works** |
208	
209	OpenCode's `gho_` token (OAuth App) works only when used *directly* as a Bearer
210	against `api.githubcopilot.com`; it cannot complete copilot-api's classic
211	token-exchange step. **Let `copilot-proxy auth` mint its own `ghu_` token — do not
212	reuse OpenCode's.** Token is stored at `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`.
213	
214	## Available Claude model ids
215	
216	Verified via `/v1/models` (2026-07): `claude-opus-4.5`, `claude-opus-4.6`,
217	`claude-opus-4.7`, `claude-opus-4.8`, `claude-sonnet-4.5`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`,
218	`claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4.5`. Non-Claude models (gpt-5.5,
219	gemini-3.1-pro-preview, …) are also served — see `copilot-model -l` or
220	`GET /v1/models`.
221	
222	## Useful commands
223	
224	```sh
225	claude-copilot                       # one-off proxy session (specstory-wrapped)
226	copilot-here status                  # is this project pinned to the proxy?
227	copilot-model -c                     # current model + which layer it came from
228	copilot-proxy status                 # up? which Claude models?
229	copilot-proxy whoami                 # validate token → account / plan / quota
230	copilot-proxy logs 60                # tail the proxy log
231	# usage dashboard:
232	#   https://ericc-ch.github.io/copilot-api?endpoint=http://localhost:4141/usage
233	```
234	
235	## See also
236	
237	- [copilot-api](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api) — the proxy
238	- [`bunx` CLI aliases](../shells/aliases.md#copilot--claude-code-proxy)
239	- [Claude Code settings precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) — why
240	  `settings.local.json` / env vars are the right injection layers
241	- [Agent overlays](agent-overlays.md) — the chezmoi-managed `~/.claude/settings.json`
242	  this design deliberately stays out of
243	- OpenCode's native GitHub Copilot provider (no proxy needed for OpenCode itself)

Both questions answered. Here's the summary — and note there's a churn issue worth flagging in the SpecStory config.

## 1. Timeout bump — committed ✅

`0b6ecf2` — `docs.yml` deploy timeout raised 10m → 20m (`timeout: 1200000`). Pre-commit passed. Only that file was committed; the other working-tree changes were left alone.

## 2. SpecStory config review — ⚠️ 有個 churn 問題

你打開的 `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`(chezmoi 管理)本身沒問題,但 **它現在有未提交的 diff,而且是 SpecStory CLI 自己寫回去的執行期狀態**:

```toml
[resume]
view_mode = "dense"
last_agent = "claude"
```

- `[providers]` 那段(YOLO-mode 各 agent 指令)是你有意設定的,沒問題。
- 但 **`[resume]` 這段是 CLI 執行 `specstory resume` 時自動寫回的 UI 狀態**,不是你配置的。這是這個檔第一次出現這種 block(`git log` 確認過:歷史上 `[resume]` 出現次數 = 0)。

**問題**:因為這是 chezmoi 管理的檔,每次你用 `specstory resume` 切換 view/agent,它就會改寫這幾行 → 造成 chezmoi 永久 drift,你每次 `chezmoi apply` 都要面對這個雜訊。

5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable

23	  applied to a new project

25	- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
26	  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
68	
69	```bash
70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
74	```
75	
76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
77	future invocations.
78	
79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
89	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
90	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
91	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
92	
93	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
94	
95	### 4. Scaffold
96	
97	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
98	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
99	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
100	copy-to-llm.
101	
102	```bash
103	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
104	  --site-name "My Project" \
105	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
106	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
107	```
108	
109	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
110	files unless `--force` is passed.
111	
112	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
113	
114	```bash
115	uv sync --extra docs
116	uv run mkdocs build --strict
117	```
118	
119	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
120	
121	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
122	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
123	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
124	Only proceed on explicit yes.
125	
126	```bash
127	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
128	  --repo owner/repo
129	```
130	
131	Flags:
132	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
133	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
134	
135	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
136	in preferences.
137	
138	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
139	
140	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
141	`mkdocs.yml`:
142	
143	```bash
144	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
145	  --section workflows \
146	  --title "My new workflow" \
147	  --slug my-new-workflow
148	```
149	
150	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
151	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
152	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
153	
154	If the project has additional languages configured in
155	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
156	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
157	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
158	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
159	
160	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
161	
162	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
163	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
164	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
165	
166	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
167	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
168	
169	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
170	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
171	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
172	
173	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
174	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
175	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
176	`Makefile` for you):
177

179	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
180	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
181	```
182	
183	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
184	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
185	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
186	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
187	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
188	is a no-op.
189	
190	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
191	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
192	
193	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
194	
195	```bash
196	uv sync --extra docs
197	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
198	```
199	
200	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
201	
202	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
203	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
204	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
205	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
206	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
207	canonical).
208	
209	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
210	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
211	
212	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
213	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
214	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
215	> invent translations)."
216	
217	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
218	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
219	
220	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
221	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
222	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
223	user may want one without the other.
224	
225	## Available scripts
226	
227	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
228	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
229	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
230	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
231	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
232	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
233	    `--no-workflow`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
234	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
235	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
236	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
237	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page and insert it into
238	  `mkdocs.yml`'s nav. If multiple languages are configured, also writes
239	  `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
240	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
241	    (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
242	- **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
243	  existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
244	  the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
245	  dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
246	  with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
247	  - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
248	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
249	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.
250	
251	## Reference files
252	
253	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
254	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
255	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
256	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
257	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
258	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
259	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
260	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
261	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
262	- `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
263	  `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
264	  the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
265	- `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
266	  `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
267	  Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
268	  caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
269	  build is on 1.x.
270	
271	## Bundled assets
272	
273	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
274	
275	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
276	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
277	  `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`.
278	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
279	  optional-deps group.
280	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
281	  paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy.
282	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
283	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
284	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
285	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
286	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
287	  terminology-rule admonition.
288	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
289	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
290	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
291	
292	## Gotchas
293	
294	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
295	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
296	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
297	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
298	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
299	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
300	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
301	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
302	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
303	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
304	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
305	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
306	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
307	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
308	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
309	  Counter-intuitive name.
310	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
311	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
312	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
313	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
314	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
315	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
316	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
317	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
318	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
319	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
320	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
321	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
322	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
323	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
324	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
325	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
326	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
327	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
328	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
329	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
330	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
331	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
332	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
333	  is just acting on it.
334	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
335	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
336	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
337	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
338	
339	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
340	
341	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
342	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
343	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
344	have customizations the templates don't know about.
345
```

10	- Linux: GitHub release tarball installed to `~/.local/bin`
11	
12	## Global vs Project Config
13	
14	This dotfiles repo manages the user-level SpecStory config at `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`.
15	
16	SpecStory reads configuration in this order:
17	
18	1. User-level config: `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`
19	2. Project-level config: `./.specstory/cli/config.toml`
20	3. CLI flags passed to `specstory`
21	
22	Later sources override earlier ones. That means the dotfile provides global defaults, while a repo-specific `.specstory/cli/config.toml` can override them when a project needs different behavior.
23	
24	## Managed Defaults
25	
26	The managed config keeps the upstream sample sections as commented documentation, but only enables `[providers]` defaults.
27	
28	Configured providers:
29	
30	- `claude_cmd = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions"`
31	- `codex_cmd = 'codex -c model_reasoning_effort="high" --ask-for-approval never --sandbox danger-full-access -c model_reasoning_summary="detailed" -c model_supports_reasoning_summaries=true'`
32	- `cursor_cmd = "cursor-agent --yolo"`
33	- `droid_cmd = "droid --yolo"`
34	- `gemini_cmd = "gemini --sandbox=none"`
35	
36	These are the commands `specstory run claude`, `specstory run codex`, and similar provider shortcuts will execute by default unless overridden per project or on the command line.
37	
38	## Safety Tradeoff
39	
40	The configured provider commands intentionally favor low-friction agent execution:
41	
42	- Claude uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
43	- Codex uses `--ask-for-approval never` and `--sandbox danger-full-access`
44	- Cursor and Droid use `--yolo`
45	- Gemini uses `--sandbox=none`
46	
47	This removes most interactive permission prompts, which is useful for fast local workflows, but it also gives the wrapped agents broader filesystem or command access. Keep these defaults only if you trust the environment and want convenience over stricter guardrails. If not, override the relevant provider command in the global file, a project-local config, or the `specstory run -c ...` flag.

## 🔎 OG tags — 現況調查

我直接 curl 了線上頁面的 `<head>`,實際只吐出**一個** meta:

```html
<meta name="description" content="Documentation for daviddwlee84/dotfiles">
```

**完全沒有任何 `og:*` 或 `twitter:*` tag。** 你 Discord 截圖看到的那個 embed 之所以還有標題/描述,是平台在硬吃 `<title>` 和這個 `name="description"` 的 fallback。問題有三層:

1. **描述是通用的** — 每一頁都是同一句 `Documentation for daviddwlee84/dotfiles`(來自 `site_description`),不是頁面專屬。
2. **沒有正規 OG tag** — Discord/Slack/Twitter 拿不到 `og:title`/`og:description`/`og:url`,只能猜。
3. **沒有預覽圖** — 沒 `og:image`,所以永遠是純文字條,不會變成漂亮的卡片。

> 註:bootstrap skill 的 `mkdocs.yml.template` 裡那個 `social:` 只是**頁尾的社群連結圖示**,跟 OG/social-cards 無關。所以 skill 目前也沒處理這塊。

## 三種做法(有真實取捨)

| 方案 | 得到什麼 | 代價 |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Material `social` 外掛** | 自動幫每頁生成 OG 卡片圖 + 完整 og/twitter meta。最漂亮。 | CI 要裝 **cairo/pango** 系統依賴(apt/brew),本地 build 也要。跟這個 repo「對安裝機制很謹慎」的哲學有點衝突。 |
| **B. 輕量組合** `mkdocs-meta-descriptions`(純 Python,自動抓每頁第一段當描述)+ 一個小 `overrides/main.html` 塞 og:title/description/url + 一張固定 og:image | 各平台都變成正規卡片、描述變頁面專屬、有統一預覽圖。約 80% 效果。 | 零系統依賴,幾乎零維護。要自備一張 og 圖。 |
| **C. 最小** 只加 `mkdocs-meta-descriptions` | 只讓文字描述變頁面專屬。 | 仍無卡片圖。改動最小。 |

我的建議:**B** —— 對一個 dotfiles 文件站,cairo/pango 進 CI 的維護成本(A)不太划算,而 B 幾乎拿到 A 的社群分享體驗又不碰系統依賴。

要往下走的話,我想先跟你確認方向:

210	if [ "$HAS_INSTANT" = "true" ]; then
211	  log "Removing navigation.instant / navigation.instant.progress (incompatible with i18n language switcher)..."
212	  yq_inplace '.theme.features |= ((. // []) - ["navigation.instant", "navigation.instant.progress"])'
213	fi
214	
215	# --- Step 2c: handle mkdocs-llmstxt incompatibility ---
216	# mkdocs-llmstxt resolves source URIs against the page index, which
217	# mkdocs-static-i18n's reconfigure_material remaps. Result: every entry in
218	# llmstxt.sections triggers a "Page URI not found" warning, which aborts
219	# `mkdocs build --strict`. Auto-discovery isn't an option (sections: is
220	# required by the llmstxt schema).
221	# Default: KEEP llmstxt — most users opted into this skill BECAUSE of the
222	# /llms.txt feature. Pair with --drop-strict to neutralise the warnings in
223	# CI. --remove-llmstxt is the opt-out for users who'd rather keep --strict.
224	HAS_LLMSTXT=$(yq '[.plugins[]? | select(has("llmstxt"))] | length > 0' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
225	if [ "$HAS_LLMSTXT" = "true" ]; then
226	  if [ "$REMOVE_LLMSTXT" = "1" ]; then
227	    log "Removing mkdocs-llmstxt plugin entry (--remove-llmstxt)..."
228	    yq_inplace 'del(.plugins[] | select(has("llmstxt")))'
229	  else
230	    log "Keeping mkdocs-llmstxt (default). 'mkdocs build --strict' will fail"
231	    log "  with 'Page URI not found' warnings — pair with --drop-strict, or"
232	    log "  drop --strict from your CI manually."
233	  fi
234	fi
235	
236	# --- Step 2d: optionally drop --strict from CI files ---
237	if [ "$DROP_STRICT" = "1" ]; then
238	  for ci_file in "$TARGET/.github/workflows/docs.yml" "$TARGET/Makefile"; do
239	    [ -f "$ci_file" ] || continue
```

```text
292	## Gotchas
293	
294	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
295	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
296	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
297	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
298	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
299	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
300	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
301	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
302	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
303	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
304	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
305	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
306	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
307	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
308	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
309	  Counter-intuitive name.
```
